q.s: A newborn born at 30 weeks to a mother with poorly controlled diabetes has grunting, nasal flaring and intercostal retractions within an hour of birth. Chest x-ray shows a diffuse ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms. The delivery was by cesarean section without labor.
o: Deficiency of surfactant from immature type II pneumocytes
e: Wrong. Possible, but not the classic picture.
q.ch: Prematurity + maternal diabetes + C-section + ground-glass CXR → surfactant deficiency → neonatal RDS.
q.tr: Maternal glucocorticoids before delivery reduce the risk.
q.q2: What is the underlying cause of his respiratory distress?
q.fc: Amniotic fluid lecithin and sphingomyelin across gestation

q.s: A pregnant woman at 31 weeks has preterm contractions. Amniocentesis is done to assess fetal lung maturity. Her obstetrician reviews the expected changes in amniotic fluid phospholipids shown.
q.ch: Lecithin rises after ~32 weeks while sphingomyelin stays flat → L/S ≥2 around 35 weeks → mature surfactant.
q.tr: An L/S ratio below 1.5 predicts neonatal RDS.
q.q2: At which gestational age does the lecithin-to-sphingomyelin ratio first reach about 2, indicating mature lungs?

q.s: A newborn becomes cyanotic every time he feeds and turns pink when he cries. A nasogastric tube cannot be passed beyond the back of the nose. He also has a coloboma of the left iris and a ventricular septal defect.
cl: cannot be passed beyond the back of the nose
q.ch: Bilateral choanal atresia + coloboma + heart defect → CHARGE → ear and genitourinary defects, growth delay.
q.tr: Diagnosis is confirmed by CT.
q.q2: Which additional finding is most likely?

q.s: A 4-year-old boy is brought in after choking on a peanut while sitting at the dinner table. He has a persistent cough and unilateral wheeze. Chest x-ray shows hyperinflation of one lower lobe.
o: The right main bronchus is longer and narrower
The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical
The carina lies to the right of midline
The heart compresses the right bronchus
The left lung has more lobes
The right lung has fewer cilia
cl: Upright aspiration goes to right lower lobe.
q.ch: Upright aspiration → right main bronchus (wider, shorter, more vertical) → right lower lobe.
q.tr: Lying supine sends material to the superior segment of the right lower lobe.
q.q2: Why is the right lung the more likely site?

q.s: A 54-year-old woman has a right pleural effusion. The physician plans thoracentesis in the midscapular line at the 8th intercostal space. She asks why the needle is placed just above the 9th rib rather than below the 8th rib.
o: The intercostal vein, artery and nerve running in the costal groove
q.ch: Intercostal neurovascular bundle runs along the inferior border of each rib → insert needle above the rib.
q.tr: Going below the 9th rib risks the liver or spleen.
q.q2: Which structures are being protected?

q.s: A 62-year-old woman with gallstones has right upper quadrant pain and fever. She also complains of pain at the tip of her right shoulder. Ultrasound shows an inflamed gallbladder touching the diaphragm.
cl: right upper quadrant pain and fever
q.ch: Diaphragm irritation → phrenic afferents (C3–C5) → pain referred to shoulder.
q.tr: "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive."
q.q2: Which nerve carries the referred shoulder pain?
q.fc: Forced expiratory spirometry, patient vs predicted

q.s: A 66-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history has progressive dyspnea on exertion and a chronic morning cough. He has a barrel chest and distant breath sounds. His spirometry is shown.
o: Decreased total lung capacity and decreased DLCO
Increased total lung capacity and decreased DLCO
Normal total lung capacity and increased DLCO
Decreased total lung capacity and normal DLCO
q.ch: FEV1 1.4/FVC 3.5 = 0.4 → obstruction + barrel chest → emphysema → ↑ TLC, ↑ RV, ↓ DLCO.
q.tr: Chronic bronchitis is a clinical diagnosis: cough ≥3 months in 2 consecutive years.
q.q2: Which set of additional findings is most likely?
q.fc: Family pedigree with protease inhibitor (Pi) phenotypes; the proband is marked with an arrow

q.s: A 38-year-old man who has never smoked has worsening dyspnea. CT shows panacinar emphysema in the lower lobes. He also has elevated liver enzymes, and liver biopsy shows PAS-positive globules in hepatocytes. His family's phenotypes are shown.
o: Type I hypersensitivity to inhaled antigens
Unopposed neutrophil elastase from deficient α1-antitrypsin
Defective chloride channel causing thick mucus
cl: panacinar emphysema in the lower lobes
Misfolded α1-antitrypsin retained in the liver.
q.ch: Nonsmoker + lower-lobe panacinar emphysema + liver disease + PiZZ → α1-antitrypsin deficiency → unopposed elastase.
q.tr: Inheritance is autosomal codominant.
q.q2: What is the mechanism of his lung disease?

q.s: A 9-year-old girl has episodes of wheezing and cough at night and after soccer practice. She has eczema and seasonal allergies. Between episodes, spirometry is normal, but FEV1 drops by 25% after inhaled methacholine.
cl: at night and after soccer practice
q.ch: Atopic child + episodic wheeze + positive methacholine challenge → asthma → eosinophil crystals and mucus spirals.
q.tr: Asthma is a type I hypersensitivity reaction.
q.q2: Which finding would most likely be seen in her sputum during an attack?

q.s: A 45-year-old woman with asthma has nasal polyps. One hour after taking aspirin for a headache, she develops severe wheezing and nasal congestion.
o: Leukotriene receptor antagonists such as montelukast
q.ch: COX inhibition → arachidonic acid shunted to 5-lipoxygenase → leukotriene excess → bronchoconstriction → block with montelukast.
q.tr: Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase but is hepatotoxic.
q.q2: Which drug class best targets the mechanism of this reaction?

q.s: A 24-year-old man with cystic fibrosis has had a chronic cough with large volumes of foul, purulent sputum every day for years. He has digital clubbing. CT shows dilated, thick-walled airways that do not taper toward the periphery.
o: Infection with impaired clearance causing permanent airway dilation
Destruction of alveolar walls by elastase
q.ch: CF → thick mucus, impaired clearance → recurrent infection and inflammation → permanently dilated bronchi.
q.tr: Clubbing occurs in bronchiectasis but not in uncomplicated COPD.
q.q2: Which process caused these airway changes?

q.s: A 70-year-old former shipyard worker has progressive dyspnea. Imaging shows fibrosis of the lower lobes and calcified pleural plaques on the diaphragm. Bronchoalveolar lavage shows golden-brown rods that stain with Prussian blue.
cl: golden-brown rods that stain with Prussian blue
q.ch: Asbestos exposure → lower-lobe fibrosis + pleural plaques → lung carcinoma risk > mesothelioma.
q.tr: Smoking multiplies the risk of bronchogenic carcinoma but not of mesothelioma.
q.q2: Which malignancy is he at highest risk of developing?

q.s: A 50-year-old man who worked for 25 years sandblasting has dyspnea and cough. Chest x-ray shows nodules in the upper lobes and eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes.
cl: eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes
q.ch: Silica disrupts macrophage phagolysosomes → impaired killing of mycobacteria → ↑ TB risk.
q.tr: Silicosis also increases risk of lung cancer and cor pulmonale.
q.q2: Which infection is he at particularly increased risk of?

q.s: A 29-year-old Black woman has a dry cough and painful red nodules on both shins. She also has blurry vision with red eyes. Chest x-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Serum calcium is 11.4 mg/dL.
o: PTHrP secreted by a lung tumor
cl: painful red nodules on both shins
q.ch: Noncaseating granulomas → macrophage 1α-hydroxylase → ↑ calcitriol → ↑ calcium absorption → hypercalcemia.
q.tr: BAL shows an elevated CD4/CD8 ratio.
q.q2: What explains her hypercalcemia?

q.s: A 58-year-old man who keeps pigeons has had progressive dyspnea and dry cough for a year. Symptoms improve when he travels away from home. CT shows ground-glass opacities and centrilobular nodules. Biopsy shows poorly formed noncaseating granulomas and alveolar septal thickening.
o: Mixed type III and IV hypersensitivity
cl: improve when he travels away from home
q.ch: Inhaled avian antigen → immune complexes and T-cell response → hypersensitivity pneumonitis (bird fancier's lung).
q.tr: Treatment is antigen avoidance, plus steroids if severe.
q.q2: Which immune mechanism is responsible?

q.s: A 45-year-old man is in the ICU 2 days after severe acute pancreatitis. He becomes progressively hypoxemic on high-flow oxygen. Chest x-ray shows bilateral diffuse opacities. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular function, and the pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is 10 mm Hg. His PaO2/FIO2 ratio is 140.
o: Alveoli filled with lysed RBCs and fibrin
q.ch: Pancreatitis → cytokines, neutrophils → endothelial damage → protein-rich edema → hyaline membranes → ARDS.
q.tr: Ventilate with low tidal volumes and higher PEEP.
q.q2: Which histologic finding is expected in his lungs?

q.s: A 22-year-old man is found unresponsive at a party with pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 6/min. His arterial blood gas is shown.
o: Hypoventilation with a normal A-a gradient
e: Wrong. A-a gradient would be high.
Wrong. A-a gradient would be high.
Wrong. A-a gradient would be high.
Wrong. Room air at sea level.
q.ch: PAO2 = 150 − 60/0.8 = 75; A-a = 75 − 64 = 11 (normal) → hypoxemia from hypoventilation.
q.tr: Naloxone reverses opioid respiratory depression.
q.q2: What is the cause of his hypoxemia?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea 10 days after a long-haul flight. She takes an estrogen-containing oral contraceptive. Her heart rate is 118/min and oxygen saturation is 89%. Breath sounds are normal.
o: V/Q of zero, like a shunt
V/Q of 3, as at the apex
V/Q of 0.6, as at the lung base
cl: sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea
q.ch: DVT risk factors → pulmonary embolism → ventilated but unperfused lung → V/Q → ∞.
q.tr: Supplemental O2 improves PaO2 in dead space but not in a true shunt.
q.q2: What is the V/Q status of the affected lung region?
q.fc: Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curves before (Curve 1) and during (Curve 2) an intervention

q.s: A 25-year-old marathon runner has blood samples drawn at rest and again near the end of a race. The hemoglobin–oxygen dissociation curves from the two samples are shown.
o: Increased temperature, CO2 and H+ in exercising muscle
cl: near the end of a race
q.ch: Exercise → ↑ temperature, CO2, H+ → right shift (P50 27 → 37 mm Hg) → more O2 unloading.
q.tr: Fetal Hb, CO and alkalosis shift the curve left.
q.q2: Which change explains the shift from Curve 1 to Curve 2?

q.s: On a cold January morning, a man and his two children come to the emergency department with headache, nausea and confusion. Their home has an old gas furnace. The father's results are shown.
o: 100% oxygen by non-rebreather mask, with hyperbaric oxygen if severe
q.ch: Multiple victims + furnace + normal PaO2 and SpO2 + high COHb → CO poisoning → 100% O2 shortens COHb half-life.
q.tr: Pulse oximetry cannot distinguish COHb from oxyhemoglobin.
q.q2: What is the best next step in treatment?

q.s: A 68-year-old man with a hypertensive emergency has received a high-dose nitroprusside infusion for 3 days. He becomes confused and develops seizures. ABG shows an anion gap metabolic acidosis with a normal PaO2, and his venous blood is unusually bright red.
cl: venous blood is unusually bright red
q.ch: Nitroprusside → cyanide → blocks complex IV → lactic acidosis, high venous O2 → hydroxocobalamin.
q.tr: Sodium thiosulfate converts cyanide to thiocyanate.
q.q2: Which drug should be given?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman with leprosy starts dapsone. Two days later she has dyspnea and gray-blue lips. Pulse oximetry reads 85% and does not improve with supplemental oxygen. Her PaO2 is 98 mm Hg, and her blood looks chocolate brown.
o: Oxidation of heme iron to Fe3+
Reduction of heme iron to Fe2+
cl: does not improve with supplemental oxygen
q.ch: Dapsone oxidizes Fe2+ → Fe3+ → methemoglobin cannot carry O2 and shifts curve left → cyanosis.
q.tr: Treat with methylene blue (and vitamin C).
q.q2: What is the mechanism of her hypoxia?

q.s: A 26-year-old climber flies from sea level to a town at 3800 m. On the second day he has headache, nausea and poor sleep. ABG shows pH 7.50 and PaCO2 28 mm Hg.
q.ch: ↓ PIO2 → hyperventilation → respiratory alkalosis → acetazolamide induces metabolic acidosis to compensate.
q.tr: Chronic altitude causes ↑ EPO and ↑ 2,3-BPG.
q.q2: Which drug would help him acclimatize faster?

q.s: A 58-year-old woman with long-standing obesity (BMI 46) has daytime sleepiness and morning headaches. Her awake ABG shows pH 7.36, PaCO2 54 mm Hg and HCO3− 30 mEq/L. Lung parenchyma is normal on CT.
q.ch: Obesity + daytime hypercapnia with compensated HCO3− → obesity hypoventilation (Pickwickian) syndrome.
q.tr: Obstructive sleep apnea alone has a normal daytime PaCO2.
q.q2: What is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 34-year-old woman has progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Her mother died of the same condition. Echocardiogram shows right ventricular hypertrophy and an estimated pulmonary artery pressure of 52 mm Hg. Left heart function and lungs are normal.
cl: Her mother died of the same condition
pulmonary artery pressure of 52 mm Hg
Left heart function and lungs are normal
q.ch: Familial PAH in a young woman → inactivating BMPR2 mutation → uncontrolled smooth muscle proliferation.
q.tr: BMPR2 normally inhibits vascular smooth muscle proliferation.
q.q2: Which gene is most likely mutated?

q.s: A 66-year-old man with pneumonia has persistent fever after 5 days of antibiotics. A new left pleural effusion is drained. The results are shown.
o: Exudate; it needs drainage with a chest tube
e: Wrong. Fails Light's criteria for transudate.
cl: persistent fever after 5 days of antibiotics
q.ch: Protein ratio 0.68 (>0.5), LDH ratio 1.9 (>0.6) → exudate; low glucose, neutrophils → complicated effusion → drain.
q.tr: Transudates come from ↑ hydrostatic or ↓ oncotic pressure.
q.q2: How is the fluid classified, and what is the next step?

q.s: A 19-year-old tall, thin man who vapes has sudden right-sided chest pain and shortness of breath while studying. His vital signs are stable. There is hyperresonance and absent breath sounds over the right apex. The trachea is midline.
o: Rupture of an apical subpleural bleb
Tension physiology from a one-way valve
q.ch: Young tall thin male + vaping + sudden pleuritic pain → apical bleb rupture → primary spontaneous pneumothorax.
q.tr: Tension pneumothorax shifts the trachea away and causes shock.
q.q2: What is the most likely cause?

q.s: A 72-year-old man who had a stroke 3 weeks ago has difficulty swallowing. He now has fever and a productive cough. Chest x-ray taken while he was bedbound and lying flat shows consolidation.
o: Superior segment of the right lower lobe or posterior segment of the right upper lobe
q.ch: Dysphagia → aspiration while supine → superior segment of RLL or posterior segment of RUL.
q.tr: Upright aspiration goes to the right lower lobe base.
q.q2: Where is the consolidation most likely located?

q.s: A 50-year-old man with alcohol use disorder has 3 weeks of fever, night sweats, weight loss and foul-smelling sputum. He has poor dentition. Chest x-ray shows a thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lung.
o: Oral anaerobes such as Bacteroides, Fusobacterium and Peptostreptococcus
q.ch: Loss of consciousness + poor teeth → aspiration of anaerobes → lung abscess with air-fluid level.
q.tr: S aureus is another cause of lung abscess.
q.q2: Which organisms are most likely?

q.s: A 65-year-old smoker has 2 months of severe right shoulder pain radiating down the inner arm, and weakness of the small muscles of his hand. His right eyelid droops and his right pupil is small. He has a hoarse voice.
cl: weakness of the small muscles of his hand
right eyelid droops and his right pupil is small
q.ch: Apical lung tumor (Pancoast) → brachial plexus, stellate ganglion and recurrent laryngeal nerve compression.
q.tr: Most Pancoast tumors are non-small cell carcinomas.
q.q2: Which structure, when compressed, explains his hoarseness?

q.s: A 63-year-old man who smokes 2 packs a day has a cough and confusion. CT shows a large central mass near the left hilum with bulky mediastinal nodes. His laboratory results are shown.
o: Small dark blue cells positive for chromogranin and synaptophysin
e: Correct. Small cell carcinoma with SIADH.
q.ch: Central tumor + euvolemic hyponatremia with concentrated urine (SIADH) → small cell carcinoma → neuroendocrine cells.
q.tr: Small cell carcinoma is treated with chemotherapy, not surgery.
q.q2: Which histologic finding is expected on biopsy?

q.s: A 46-year-old woman who has never smoked has a cough. CT shows a peripheral 3-cm mass in the right upper lobe. Biopsy shows malignant glands with mucin. Molecular testing finds a targetable mutation.
q.ch: Nonsmoking woman + peripheral mucin-producing adenocarcinoma → EGFR (also KRAS, ALK) mutations.
q.tr: Adenocarcinoma is the most common primary lung cancer.
q.q2: Which mutation is most likely in this tumor?

q.s: A 70-year-old woman with lung cancer has worsening facial swelling and redness, headache and dilated veins over her chest. Her arms are swollen, but her legs are not. Pressing on her flushed face leaves a pale mark.
o: Obstruction of the superior vena cava
cl: Her arms are swollen, but her legs are not
q.ch: Lung cancer + upper body edema + facial plethora + chest collaterals → SVC syndrome.
q.tr: Severe cases raise intracranial pressure.
q.q2: What is the cause of her symptoms?

q.s: A 64-year-old smoker has a cough and fatigue. Serum calcium is 13.2 mg/dL with a low PTH. CT shows a cavitating mass near the right hilum.
o: Bone metastases from small cell carcinoma
cl: Serum calcium is 13.2 mg/dL with a low PTH
q.ch: Central cavitating tumor in a smoker + hypercalcemia with suppressed PTH → squamous cell carcinoma → PTHrP.
q.tr: Histology shows keratin pearls.
q.q2: What causes his hypercalcemia?

q.s: A 9-year-old boy with asthma uses his albuterol inhaler 5 times a week and wakes at night with cough twice a week. His pediatrician adds a daily controller medicine that inactivates NF-κB.
o: Oral thrush, reduced by a spacer and rinsing the mouth
cl: uses his albuterol inhaler 5 times a week
q.ch: Persistent asthma → inhaled glucocorticoid (first-line controller) → oral candidiasis risk.
q.tr: Inhaled steroids inhibit synthesis of most cytokines.
q.q2: Which adverse effect should the family be warned about?

q.s: A 70-year-old man with COPD takes inhaled tiotropium and salmeterol but still has frequent exacerbations with chronic bronchitis. His physician adds an oral drug that selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-4.
q.ch: COPD with chronic bronchitis and exacerbations → PDE-4 inhibitor → ↑ cAMP, ↓ inflammation.
q.tr: Triple inhaled therapy (ICS + LABA + LAMA) also reduces exacerbations.
q.q2: Which drug was added?

q.s: A 40-year-old woman has severe asthma with eosinophil counts of 900/μL despite high-dose inhaled steroids and a LABA. Her IgE is normal. She starts a monthly injection of a monoclonal antibody that binds the IL-5 receptor α.
q.ch: Severe eosinophilic asthma → anti-IL-5Rα (benralizumab) → depletes eosinophils.
q.tr: Mepolizumab and reslizumab target IL-5 itself.
q.q2: Which drug did she start?

q.s: A 45-year-old woman with pulmonary arterial hypertension starts an oral drug that competitively blocks endothelin-1 receptors. Her physician orders monthly blood tests.
q.ch: Endothelin receptor antagonist (bosentan) → hepatotoxic → monitor LFTs (also teratogenic).
q.tr: PDE-5 inhibitors are contraindicated with nitrates.
q.q2: What do the blood tests monitor?

q.s: A 3-year-old girl has progressive hoarseness and a weak cry. Laryngoscopy shows multiple wart-like growths on the true vocal cords. Her mother had genital warts at the time of delivery.
cl: progressive hoarseness and a weak cry
wart-like growths on the true vocal cords
genital warts at the time of delivery
q.ch: Child + vocal cord papillomas + maternal genital warts → recurrent respiratory papillomatosis → HPV-6/11.
q.tr: Laryngeal papillomas favor stratified squamous epithelium.
q.q2: Which viral types are responsible?

q.s: A 16-year-old boy has had repeated heavy nosebleeds from his right nostril and progressive nasal obstruction. Examination shows a reddish, vascular mass in the posterior nasal cavity.
cl: reddish, vascular mass in the posterior nasal cavity
q.ch: Adolescent male + recurrent epistaxis + posterior nasal vascular mass → nasal angiofibroma.
q.tr: Most nosebleeds come from the anterior Kiesselbach plexus.
q.q2: What is the most likely diagnosis?
